mainTopic: How the תנאים estimated time, the laws of נטילת ידים, and aggadic teachings on אשת איש and גסות הרוח
overview: The amud opens by finishing some questions about the loaf-in-the-basket time estimate, and they end in תיקו. רבי יוחנן explains that each תנא based his time estimate on his own experience. The גמרא asks how בן עזאי could do this when he never married, and gives three answers. A פסוק about a loaf of bread leads to teachings on נטילת ידים: how serious it is, how to hold the hands for מים ראשונים and מים אחרונים, and the need to dry them. רבא and רבי יוחנן then explain משלי 6:26 as a warning about the sin of אשת איש. Next come four sayings about how terrible גסות הרוח is. They compare it to עבודה זרה, to denying ה׳, to all the עריות, and to building a במה. Finally, רב, the school of רבי שילא, and רבי יוחנן each explain the words 'יד ליד לא ינקה'. רבי יוחנן's own explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: More details about the loaf of bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues an earlier string of questions about the estimate of taking a loaf from a basket. Was it a wheat loaf or a barley loaf? Was it soft or hard?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we talking about a wheat loaf or a barley loaf? A soft loaf or a hard one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing a list of questions that began before this section, asking exactly what kind of loaf the time estimate is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion measured the time by how long it takes to reach into a basket and take out a loaf. The kind of bread changes how long that takes. A soft loaf might catch on the side of the basket, and wheat and barley loaves come out differently. So the גמרא wants to know which case sets the measurement.
steps.confusionAlert: These questions are not about food laws. They only ask how to measure a length of time that one opinion described using a loaf of bread.

phrases.english: With wheat bread or with barley bread?
phrases.notes: Still asking about the time it takes to eat a loaf from the basket, which came up just before this.

phrases.english: With a soft loaf or with a hard one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of questions from the previous part of the daf
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of loaf (wheat or barley, soft or hard) sets the time measurement

steps.title: The questions stay unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that these questions remain unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the list of questions by saying they stay unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the גמרא found no source to settle the questions. The exact measure in these cases stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the questions of step 1 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about the type of loaf are left unresolved.

steps.title: Each sage judged by his own experience
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains why the תנאים gave different time estimates: each one based his estimate on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר רב יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: each and every one of them estimated based on himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains where all the different time estimates came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many different measures are not really an argument about a fact. Each תנא simply measured from his own personal experience, and that is why the numbers differ.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Rav Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Each and every one,
phrases.notes: He means each of the sages who gave a time estimate earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: estimated based on himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to explain the source of all the different time estimates
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each תנא based his time estimate on his own experience.

steps.title: But בן עזאי never married
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: בן עזאי also gave an estimate, but he never married, so he could not have based it on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is בן עזאי, who did not marry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with a case that does not seem to fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every estimate came from personal experience, a sage without a wife would have no experience to measure from. בן עזאי was one of those who gave an estimate, yet he never married.

phrases.english: But there is Ben Azzai,
who did not marry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that every sage estimated based on himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן עזאי gave an estimate without ever being married, so he had no personal experience to use.

steps.title: Three ways בן עזאי could have known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three possible answers: he married and then separated, he learned it from his teacher, or Heaven revealed it to him because he feared ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say he married and then separated. If you want, say he heard it from his teacher. If you want, say: 'The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by offering three different ways to explain בן עזאי's knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer keeps רבי יוחנן's rule fully: בן עזאי did have experience for a while. The second and third answers treat בן עזאי as an exception who got the knowledge another way, either from his teacher or as a gift from ה׳ to those who fear Him.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say: he married and then separated.
And if you want, say: he heard it from his teacher.
And if you want, say: "The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him."
phrases.notes: תהלים 25:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Three alternative answers that explain how בן עזאי knew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן עזאי had no way to know, so רבי יוחנן's rule fails
steps.terutzMaskana: בן עזאי knew from brief married life, from his teacher, or by Heavenly insight.
steps.whatToRemember: The different time estimates come from each sage's own experience. בן עזאי is explained either as having briefly married or as getting the knowledge another way.

steps.title: Eating bread without washing hands
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא teaches, in the name of רבי אמי or רבי אסי, that eating bread without נטילת ידים is like being with a זונה, based on the פסוק about the loaf of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רבי אמי and sometimes in the name of רבי אסי: anyone who eats bread without washing his hands is as if he was with a זונה, as it says: 'For because of a זונה woman, down to a loaf of bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching that uses the same פסוק about a loaf of bread that the earlier time estimate used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the פסוק was used to measure a length of time. רב עוירא reads it a new way: it puts 'זונה' right next to 'loaf of bread,' so eating bread carelessly, without washing, is compared to a serious sin. The point is how serious it is to skip נטילת ידים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for how seriously חז"ל treated washing hands before eating bread.
steps.confusionAlert: 'As if' is a comparison to show how serious this is. It does not mean the two acts are the same sin in every way.

phrases.english: Rav Avira taught,

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: וְזִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Asi:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹכֵל לֶחֶם בְּלֹא נְטִילַת יָדַיִם —
phrases.english: Anyone who eats bread without washing his hands
is as if he was with a prostitute.
As it says: "For because of a prostitute,"
phrases.notes: משלי 6:26. This is the same פסוק used earlier on the daf for the loaf-of-bread time estimate.

phrases.english: "down to a loaf of bread."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected through the פסוק about a loaf of bread
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating bread without נטילת ידים is compared to being with a זונה, learned from משלי 6:26.

steps.title: רבא questions the word order of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the פסוק puts the זונה first and the bread second, so it does not fit the earlier reading that the bread leads to the זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This verse says, 'because of a harlot, to a loaf of bread.' If it meant what was just taught, it should have said, 'because of a loaf of bread, to a harlot!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is challenging the way the פסוק was just used to compare eating without washing to being with a זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading said that being careless with bread leads to the sin of a זונה. But the פסוק lists the זונה first and the bread after it. If the bread were the cause, the bread should have been mentioned first.

phrases.english: Rava said: This verse,
"For on account of a harlot, to a loaf of bread"
phrases.notes: משלי 6:26.

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּעַד כִּכַּר לֶחֶם עַד אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have said: "On account of a loaf of bread, to a harlot!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 6 read the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עוירא's reading that the loaf of bread leads to the זונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse's word order runs from זונה to bread, which is the reverse of what that reading needs.

steps.title: רבא reads the verse a new way
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the פסוק in a way that fits its order: a man who goes to a זונה ends up poor, begging for a loaf of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Anyone who is with a harlot will in the end beg for a loaf of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading of the פסוק, one that fits the word order he just pointed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse now reads as cause and effect in the right order. The sin with the זונה comes first, and poverty follows from it. The verse becomes a warning about the result of the sin, not a teaching about bread.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Anyone who has relations with a harlot
will in the end beg for a loaf of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's own question from step 7 with a new reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse teaches that carelessness with bread leads to the sin of a זונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that the sin of a זונה leads to poverty.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads the פסוק as: sin with a זונה leads a man to poverty, so he ends up begging for bread.

steps.title: Treating handwashing lightly is very serious
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person who treats נטילת ידים with contempt is uprooted from the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Anyone who treats washing hands lightly is uprooted from the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of washing hands and shows how serious it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 already compared eating without washing to a grave sin. This statement adds a severe punishment for someone who disrespects the practice. It is aimed at contempt for the מצוה, not just at forgetting once.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
Anyone who treats washing hands lightly
is uprooted from the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the verse discussion to the importance of נטילת ידים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Treating נטילת ידים with contempt brings the punishment of being uprooted from the world.

steps.title: Raising and lowering the hands when washing
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that for מים ראשונים you raise your hands upward, and for מים אחרונים you lower them downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: For the first water, a person must raise his hands upward. For the last water, he must lower his hands downward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical rule about how to hold your hands when washing before and after a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two washings: one before eating (מים ראשונים) and one after the meal, before ברכת המזון (מים אחרונים). Each one has its own way of holding the hands. The next step will give the reason for raising the hands.

keyTerms.meaning: First water: washing before the meal
Last water: washing after the meal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים — צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּגְבִּיהַּ יָדָיו לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: For the first water, he must raise his hands upward;

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים — צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּשְׁפִּיל יָדָיו לְמַטָּה.
phrases.english: for the last water, he must lower his hands downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of נטילת ידים with practical details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hands are raised after מים ראשונים and lowered after מים אחרונים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical halacha about how to wash hands properly.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports raising the hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says to raise the hands after washing, because otherwise the water could run past the washed area, become impure, and flow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: One who washes his hands must raise them upward, in case the water goes past the joint and then comes back and makes the hands impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב and also gives the reason for raising the hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hands point down, water can run beyond the part that was washed and become impure there. If the hands are then tilted, that impure water could flow back onto the clean area. Raising the hands keeps the water from flowing back the wrong way.

keyTerms.meaning: Joint (the edge of the area that is washed)

phrases.english: A ברייתא also teaches this:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹטֵל יָדָיו — צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּגְבִּיהַּ יָדָיו לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: One who washes his hands must raise his hands upward,
in case the water goes out past the joint,
phrases.notes: Past the joint is the part of the arm he did not wash, so water that reaches it becomes impure.

phrases.english: and comes back and makes the hands impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's rule from step 10 and gives its reason.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule to raise the hands after מים ראשונים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same rule, plus the reason about water flowing back.

steps.title: Eating bread without drying the hands
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that eating bread without drying your hands is like eating impure bread, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Anyone who eats bread without drying his hands is as if he is eating impure bread, as it says: 'And ה׳ said: This is how the children of Israel will eat their bread impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching about washing: you also need to dry your hands before eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing is not the end of the process; the hands must also be dried. רבי אבהו compares bread eaten with wet hands to impure bread. He uses a פסוק that calls the bread eaten in exile 'impure.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹכֵל פַּת בְּלֹא נִיגּוּב יָדַיִם —
phrases.english: Anyone who eats bread without drying his hands
is as if he is eating impure bread,
as it is said: "And ה׳ said: This is how

phrases.aramaic: יֹאכְלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת לַחְמָם טָמֵא וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: the children of Israel will eat their bread impure, etc."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 4:13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail about washing hands: drying them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating bread without drying the hands is like eating impure bread.
steps.whatToRemember: Washing hands includes three things: wash, hold the hands the right way, and dry them before eating.

steps.title: What does the second half of the verse mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק from משלי and asks what the words 'and a married woman hunts a precious soul' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'and a married woman hunts a precious soul' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוק that רבא explained and asks about its second half. It is setting up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained only the first half of the פסוק, about the זונה and the bread. Now the גמרא wants to know what the second half adds, especially the words 'precious soul.'

phrases.english: And what does "and a married woman hunts a precious soul" mean?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, משלי 6:26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק explained in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'a married woman hunts a precious soul.'

steps.title: Arrogance leads to sin with a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that a person with גסות הרוח will in the end stumble with an אשת איש, and he learns this from the second half of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any person who has arrogance will in the end stumble with a married woman, as it says: 'and a married woman hunts a precious soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining the 'precious soul' as an arrogant person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'precious soul' is someone who sees himself as precious and important. Such a person is the one the married woman 'hunts,' so his arrogance ends with this sin.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ —
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him
will in the end stumble with a married woman,
as it is said: "and a married woman hunts a precious soul."
phrases.notes: The 'precious soul' is the man who thinks highly of himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'precious soul' is the arrogant person, who in the end stumbles with an אשת איש.
steps.whatToRemember: גסות הרוח is not just a bad trait; according to רבי יוחנן, it leads to serious sin with an אשת איש.

steps.title: רבא questions how the verse was read
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises two wording problems with reading the פסוק as being about an arrogant person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the פסוק were about an arrogant person, it should have said 'a haughty soul,' not 'a precious soul.' Also, the wording of 'hunts' doesn't fit that reading either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation from the last step by pointing to the exact words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the פסוק teaches that an arrogant person ends up with an אשת איש. רבא asks: the word for arrogant would be 'גבוהה' (high), but the פסוק says 'יקרה' (precious). His second point is that the verb also doesn't match the picture of who is hunting whom.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This phrase, "a precious soul"
it should have said "a haughty soul."
And furthermore, it should have said "she hunts"!
phrases.notes: רבא means the wording of the verb doesn't match רבי יוחנן's picture of who is chasing whom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: האי נפש יקרה נפש גבוהה מיבעי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the פסוק is about a person with גסות הרוח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words of the פסוק ('יקרה' and the form of 'תצוד') do not fit a description of an arrogant person.

steps.title: רבא's own reading: even Torah won't save an adulterer
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'precious soul' means a person who learned Torah, and even he will be caught and brought to גיהנם for sinning with an אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Anyone who sins with a married woman, even if he learned Torah (which is called 'more precious than pearls,' more precious than a כהן גדול who enters the inner sanctuary), the sin will hunt him down to the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי יוחנן's reading, רבא gives his own explanation of the פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'יקרה' as pointing to Torah, which a פסוק calls 'יקרה היא מפנינים.' So the 'precious soul' is a Torah scholar. The lesson is that his Torah will not protect him; the sin of אשת איש will trap him in גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: pearls; here linked to לפני ולפנים
the innermost sanctuary, the קודש הקדשים
the place of punishment after death

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the 'precious soul' is a person who learned Torah, and even he is not protected if he sins with an אשת איש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Anyone who has relations with a married woman,
even if he learned Torah,
about which it is written "It is more precious than pearls,"
phrases.notes: משלי 3:15

phrases.english: more precious than a High Priest
phrases.notes: The גמרא hears מפנינים like לפני ולפנים, the innermost holy place where only the כהן גדול went.

phrases.english: who enters the innermost sanctuary,
"it will hunt him down"
to the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא: כל הבא על אשת איש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that רבא rejected in step 15 with his own answer to the question of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'ואשת איש נפש יקרה תצוד' mean (step 13).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a person precious through Torah learning will be trapped in the judgment of גיהנם if he sins with an אשת איש.

steps.title: Arrogance is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that an arrogant person is like one who worships עבודה זרה, learned from the shared word תועבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Any person with גסות הרוח is as if he worships idols. Here it says 'Every haughty heart is a תועבה to ה׳,' and there, about idols, it says 'Do not bring a תועבה into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: how serious גסות הרוח is. The first opinion compares it to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a word link: the word 'תועבה' appears about the arrogant person and also about idols. Since the same word is used, arrogance is treated like idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written here... and it is written there (a word link between two פסוקים)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him
is as if he worships idols.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״תּוֹעֲבַת ה׳ כׇּל גְּבַהּ לֵב״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "Every haughty heart is an abomination to ה׳,"
phrases.notes: משלי 16:5

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וְלָא תָבִיא תוֹעֵבָה אֶל בֵּיתֶךָ״.
phrases.english: and it is written there: "And do not bring an abomination into your house."
phrases.notes: דברים 7:26, talking about idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחי: כל אדם שיש בו גסות הרוח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משלי verse to a new series of sayings about the severity of arrogance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with גסות הרוח is considered like an idol worshipper, based on the shared word תועבה.

steps.title: Arrogance is like denying ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's own view: an arrogant person is as if he denied ה׳, based on a פסוק linking a raised heart to forgetting ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן himself said: An arrogant person is as if he denied the foundation of faith, as it says: 'And your heart will be raised up, and you will forget ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, רבי יוחנן's own, comparing גסות הרוח to כפירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the proof is direct, not a word link: the פסוק itself says a raised heart leads to forgetting ה׳. This is רבי יוחנן's personal view, separate from what he quoted from his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: and your heart will be raised up

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן appears twice: first quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, then giving his own different view. These are two separate opinions.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan himself said:
It is as if he denied the foundation of faith,
as it is stated: "And your heart will be raised up,
and you will forget ה׳ your God, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 8:14

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יוחנן דידיה אמר: כאילו כפר בעיקר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second comparison for arrogance, alongside the עבודה זרה comparison of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with גסות הרוח is considered as if he denied ה׳.

steps.title: Arrogance is like all the forbidden relationships
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא teaches that an arrogant person is as if he sinned with all the עריות, again using the word תועבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: An arrogant person is as if he had relations with all the forbidden women. Here it says 'Every haughty heart is a תועבה to ה׳,' and there, about the עריות, it says 'For all these תועבות...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion, comparing גסות הרוח to all the עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first opinion, this uses the word link 'תועבה,' but connects it to a different פסוק, the one closing the list of עריות. So the same word yields a different comparison.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on גסות הרוח: like עבודה זרה (רבי שמעון בן יוחי), like denying ה׳ (רבי יוחנן), like all the עריות (רבי חמא בר חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
It is as if he had relations with all the forbidden women.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״תּוֹעֲבַת ה׳ כׇּל גְּבַהּ לֵב״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "Every haughty heart is an abomination to ה׳,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״כִּי אֶת כׇּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵל וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written there: "For all these abominations, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:27, at the end of the list of עריות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי חמא בר חנינא אמר: כאילו בא על כל העריות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third comparison for arrogance, using the same word link as step 17 but with a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with גסות הרוח is considered as if he sinned with all the עריות.

steps.title: עולא: An arrogant person is like one who built an altar for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that an arrogant person is as if he built a במה, by reading the word בַּמֶּה in a פסוק as בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: An arrogant person is as if he built an altar for idol worship. The פסוק says, 'Stop relying on man, who has only breath in his nostrils, for how little (בַּמֶּה) is he worth.' Do not read it as בַּמֶּה ('how little'); read it as בָּמָה ('altar').
steps.whatsHappening: This is one more saying in the list of how serious arrogance is. עולא compares an arrogant person to someone who built an altar for idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sayings compared arrogance to עבודה זרה, to denying ה׳, and to the עריות. עולא gets his comparison by reading the letters of בַּמֶּה with different vowels, so the word becomes בָּמָה, an altar. רש״י explains that this בָּמָה is an altar for עבודה זרה, so the arrogant person is pictured as building an altar for idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: An altar; here, as רש״י explains, an altar for עבודה זרה
'In what?' or 'how little?', the plain reading of the word in the פסוק
'Do not read it as... but as...', a way of drawing a lesson by reading a word differently
As if, the person is treated as though he did this

phrases.english: Ulla said: It is as if he built an altar,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the arrogant person from the earlier sayings.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Cease you from man,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 2:22

phrases.english: in whose nostrils there is breath,
for how little is he to be accounted.'
Do not read 'bammeh' (how little), but rather 'bama' (altar).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth comparison to the list of sayings about arrogance (after רבי שמעון בן יוחי, רבי יוחנן, and רבי חמא בר חנינא).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant person is as if he built an altar for idol worship, learned by reading בַּמֶּה as בָּמָה.

steps.title: What does 'hand to hand, he shall not be unpunished' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק in משלי about the arrogant person and asks what its ending phrase means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'Hand to hand, he shall not go unpunished'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks about the ending of the same פסוק it has been explaining, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון בן יוחי and רבי חמא בר חנינא quoted the first half of this פסוק ('Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to ה׳') for their word links. Now the גמרא turns to the strange words 'hand to hand', which do not make sense on their own and need explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used to ask for the meaning of a phrase
Hand to hand, the unclear phrase being explained
He will not be cleared, he will not escape punishment

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'Hand to hand, he shall not be unpunished'?
phrases.notes: משלי 16:5, the same פסוק about the proud-hearted person the גמרא was explaining before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sayings about arrogance to explaining the second half of the פסוק in משלי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'יד ליד לא ינקה'.

steps.title: רב: Even someone like אברהם will not escape גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that one who sins with an אשת איש will not escape גיהנם, even if he raised his hand to ה׳ like אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Anyone who sins with a married woman, even if he declared that ה׳ owns heaven and earth like אברהם אבינו did (about whom it says, 'I have lifted up my hand to ה׳, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth'), will not escape the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. 'Hand' points to אברהם's hand that he raised to ה׳, and even a person with that greatness is not saved from גיהנם for this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects the word 'hand' in משלי 16:5 to the פסוק where אברהם says 'I have lifted up my hand' to ה׳. So 'hand to hand' means: even with a hand like אברהם's raised to ה׳, a man who sins with an אשת איש is not cleared. רב reads the end of this פסוק, which opened with the proud-hearted person, as a warning about the sin of אשת איש.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared ownership to Him, he proclaimed that ה׳ owns
As it is written about him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rav said: Anyone who has relations with a married woman,
even if he declared the Holy One, Blessed be He, the owner of
heaven and earth, like Avraham our father,
about whom it is written: 'I have lifted up my hand to ה׳,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:22

phrases.english: God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth' —
he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Hand' refers to אברהם's raised hand; even one as great as him will not escape גיהנם for sinning with an אשת איש.

steps.title: The school of רבי שילא: The wording should have been 'my hand'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שילא challenges רב: if the פסוק were hinting at אברהם, it should say 'my hand', not 'hand to hand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא had a difficulty: this phrase, 'hand to hand, he shall not be unpunished', should have said 'my hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי שילא challenges רב's reading. The words 'hand to hand' do not match the פסוק about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's פסוק says 'my hand', just one hand raised to ה׳. 'Hand to hand' sounds like something passing from one hand to another hand, which does not fit אברהם at all. So רב's link between the two פסוקים looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי שילא

steps.confusionAlert: They are not arguing about the law. Everyone agrees this sinner is not saved from גיהנם; they are only arguing about which great person the word 'hand' points to.

phrases.english: It was difficult for the school of Rabbi Sheila:
This phrase, 'hand to hand, he shall not be unpunished,'
it should have said 'my hand'!
phrases.notes: 'My hand' is the word used in אברהם's פסוק, so that is what they would expect if it were hinting at him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's explanation from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's link between 'יד ליד' and אברהם's 'הרימותי ידי'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording does not match: אברהם's פסוק says 'my hand', while משלי says 'hand to hand', so the hint must be to something else.

steps.title: The school of רבי שילא: Even someone like משה who received the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שילא explains 'hand to hand' as the Torah passed from ה׳'s hand to משה's hand; even one with that greatness will not escape גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the school of רבי שילא said: Even if he received the Torah like משה רבינו, about whom it is written, 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them', he will not escape the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי שילא gives its own explanation of 'hand to hand'. It points to משה receiving the Torah from ה׳'s hand into his own hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading fits the wording better: 'hand to hand' is the Torah passing from ה׳'s right hand to משה's hand. The lesson stays the same as רב's: even a person of the highest greatness is not saved from גיהנם if he sins with an אשת איש.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, they say, bringing a new explanation in place of the old one

steps.whatToRemember: 'יד ליד לא ינקה' teaches that sinning with an אשת איש leads to גיהנם no matter how great the person is. רב compares him to אברהם; the school of רבי שילא, because of the wording 'hand to hand', compares him to משה receiving the Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא pays close attention to each word of a פסוק: one small wording detail ('hand to hand' and not 'my hand') changes which hint is being made.

phrases.english: Rather, the school of Rabbi Sheila said:
Even if he received the Torah like Moshe our teacher,
about whom it is written: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them' —
phrases.notes: דברים 33:2. The Torah went from ה׳'s hand into משה's hand, and that's the 'hand to hand'.

phrases.english: he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב's reading after the wording challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the explanation with one that fits the wording better
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Hand' refers to אברהם's single raised hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Hand to hand' refers to the Torah passing from ה׳'s hand to משה's hand; even such a person is not saved from גיהנם for sinning with an אשת איש.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's problem with the 'Torah from hand to hand' reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges the school of רבי שילא. If the פסוק meant the Torah passing from ה׳ to משה, it should say 'hand from hand,' not 'hand to hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult for רבי יוחנן: this phrase 'hand to hand'? It should have said 'hand from hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי יוחנן was bothered by the explanation of the school of רבי שילא from the last step. The words of the פסוק don't fit their reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רבי שילא said 'hand to hand' means the Torah went from ה׳'s hand to משה's hand. רבי יוחנן points out that when you describe receiving something from someone, the natural wording is 'hand from hand.' Since the פסוק says 'hand to hand,' their reading doesn't match the words.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him. Someone finds a problem with an explanation.
'Hand to hand.' The words actually written in the פסוק in משלי.
'Hand from hand.' The wording רבי יוחנן says would fit receiving something from someone.
It should have said. The text ought to have used different words.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of challenge the school of רבי שילא brought against רב in step 23. Now their own explanation gets challenged the same way, by looking closely at the exact words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: It is difficult for Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: He's bothered by the explanation from the school of רבי שילא in the step before.

phrases.english: this phrase "hand to hand"?
It should have said "hand from hand"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given by the school of רבי שילא in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The school of רבי שילא's reading that 'hand to hand' means the Torah passed from ה׳'s hand to משה's hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Receiving something from someone would be written 'hand from hand.' The פסוק says 'hand to hand,' so it is probably not describing receiving the Torah.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן begins his own explanation
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected the earlier readings, רבי יוחנן starts to give his own explanation of 'hand to hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The word אֶלָּא tells us the earlier reading is being dropped, and the גמרא is getting ready to bring רבי יוחנן's new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier readings, רב's (אברהם) and the school of רבי שילא's (משה receiving the Torah), had problems with the exact wording. רבי יוחנן now offers a third way to read the פסוק. His actual explanation comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous idea is dropped and a new one is coming.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the challenge in step 25 by bringing in a new reading to replace the rejected one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This line only introduces רבי יוחנן's new explanation of 'hand to hand.' The content comes in the next line.
